# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-256 of cycle-129: implement-gate modes (ask/telemetry/deny with marker and derived-cache sanctions), the file-authoritative run position in `run-checkpoint.sh` (`derive`, `record-round`, `mark`), the fail-closed heredoc consumer classifier in the Bash fence, the `loa.profile` resolver (`profile-lib.sh`), the per-task Karpathy surgical hook, the Agent Teams table pruning and the prose diet. The design is coherent and most of it is well tested: the implement-gate matrix (IG-24..33), `profile-lib.bats` (17/17), `lint-invariants.bats` (9/9), the fence corpus (benign 89/89, dangerous 142/142, p95 76 ms) and the karpathy suites all pass on the head tree.

Two defects block the merge. First, the heredoc classifier has a same-command execution bypass: a heredoc written to a plain file and executed in the *same* Bash command through a glob, `cat file | bash`, `bash <(cat file)`, `bash -c "$(cat file)"`, an indirect variable or `make` is classified non-executing, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` then drops every body segment that does not start with a fence verb. Six such commands that the base fence blocks (FR-SZ2-REDIR, a floor fence) are allowed by the head fence. Second, `run-checkpoint.sh derive` and `record-round` are broken on jq 1.6: the per-sprint jq uses `$label` (a jq keyword, rejected by jq 1.6) and `fb_parse` relies on `jq -e` exiting non-zero on empty input (jq 1.6 exits 0), so `derive` exits 3 on every ledger and `record-round` exits 2 on any trailer-less feedback file. The derive suite fails 17/22 and `record-round` 1/8 in this environment (jq-1.6, Debian). The repository states no jq floor, and every other script in the tree runs on 1.6.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — heredoc classifier: same-command execution bypass of a floor fence

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only recognises an executing reference when a later token's literal basename equals the heredoc target; a glob (`bash ./ru[n]`, `bash n.m?`), a pipe from a safe reader (`cat n.md | bash`), a process or command substitution (`bash <(cat n.md)`, `bash -c "$(cat n.md)"`), an indirect variable (`f=n.md; bash $f`) or a consumer that does not name the file (`make` after `cat > Makefile`) is missed, the heredoc stays `nonexec`, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576`) drops every body line whose command word is not a fence verb. The written body then executes in the same command unseen.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-639` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), `:222-227` (`_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` lists `cat`, `git`, `gh`), `:576-600` (`_bdb_hd_scan_body`), `:538-574` (`_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip `if/then/do/else/elif/while/until` or case arms)
**Issue:** Reproduced end to end by feeding Bash-tool payloads to the head and base hooks (exit 0 = allow, 2 = block):

```
head=0 base=2 | cat > run <<'EOF' / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / bash ./ru[n]
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / cat n.md | bash
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash <(cat n.md)
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash -c "$(cat n.md)"
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / f=n.md; bash $f
head=0 base=2 | cat > Makefile <<'EOF' / all: / <tab>cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh / EOF / make
head=2 base=2 | control: … / EOF / bash n.md            (D119 shape, caught)
head=2 base=2 | control: body `rm -rf src` is kept as a fence-verb segment
```

The body content that disappears is exactly the class the fence-verb keep does not cover: `echo … > .claude/settings.json` (FR-SZ2-REDIR), `cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh` (FR-SZ-COPY), `tee`, `ln`, `sed -i` into the System Zone, and any destructive segment prefixed by a shell keyword (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `for f in src; do rm -rf $f; done` — both scrub to nothing, verified with `_bdb_heredoc_scrub`). FR-SZ and FR-SZ2 are `floor_guards` in `.claude/data/floor.yaml`; the hooks-reference "Remaining gap" (`head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:298`) covers only execution by a *later* command, so this is a regression inside the fence's own stated scope, not the documented gap.
**Why This Matters:** The classifier is on by default (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: true`). An autonomous agent that writes a helper file with a heredoc and runs it in the same command no longer has its body scanned, and the pre-cycle fence did scan it. The corpus (D119–D121) only covers the literal-basename shapes.
**Required Fix:** (1) In `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`, treat any non-body line holding `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a glob character in a token, or a `$`-prefixed token as executing (return 0), mirroring `_bdb_hd_ctx_bad`; remove `cat`, `git` and `gh` from `_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` when the segment is a pipeline member feeding an interpreter, or simply fall back to the full scan whenever any later segment's command word is an interpreter/wrapper (`_bdb_hd_is_interp`) regardless of whether it names the target. (2) In `_bdb_hd_segword`, strip the shell keywords (`if then else elif fi while until do done case esac select in coproc function`) and a leading case-arm pattern before reading the command word, or set `_hd_full=1` in `_bdb_hd_scan_body` when a segment's command word is a keyword. (3) Add corpus rows for each of the six shapes above (expect `block`) and for `cat <<EOF > notes.md` with an `if …; then rm -rf …; fi` body.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); the fence's own posture note (`hooks-reference.md:287`) accepts subshell wrapping as a bypass class for the *whole command*, not for a heredoc body the fence previously scanned.

### 2. Functionality — `run-checkpoint.sh derive` / `record-round` fail on jq 1.6

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` — the per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and reads `$label` (`:380`, `:389`); `label` is a jq keyword and jq 1.6 rejects it (`syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__`), so `cmd_derive` exits 3 before producing any report, on every ledger.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-395` and `:225-226`
**Issue:** Reproduced with the RCD-1 fixture (`bash -x`): `jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label … line 2: def mine: … $label` → `sj=` → exit 3. Minimal: `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` fails on jq-1.6 and works on 1.7. A second 1.6 incompatibility sits in `fb_parse` (`:225-226`): for a feedback file without a trailer `pj` is empty, and `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"` exits 0 on empty input under jq 1.6 (verified: `printf '' | jq -e 'type == "object"'; echo $?` → 0), so `pj` stays `""`, `--argjson p ''` fails with `invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`, `fb_parse` prints nothing and `record-round` exits 2 (`set -e`) on any legacy feedback file; `derive` would hit the same path on RCD-3. Test evidence on the head tree (jq-1.6): `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` 17/22 fail (RCD-1..12, 14, 15, 17, R1, R4, R5), `run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` RCR-7 fails; the RCR-1..6 cases that never reach a legacy file pass.
**Why This Matters:** `derive` is the file-authoritative run position this sprint ships. On a jq 1.6 host it is inert: every `run-checkpoint.sh write` and `mark` prints the derive error to stderr (`:174`, `:541`), `/loa`'s Run line is silently skipped, `/run-resume` step 0a gets exit 3 (its contract handles only 4), and the implement gate's `deny` mode never sees a `derived_at`, so it can only ever ask. The repository documents no jq minimum, and the rest of the tree (including the implement gate and the fence) runs on 1.6.
**Required Fix:** Rename the binding (`--arg lbl` / `$lbl`, or `--arg local_label`) and avoid other jq keywords as variable names; replace the `jq -e` emptiness probe with an explicit test (`[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`); either declare a jq ≥ 1.7 floor in the framework prerequisites and have `run-checkpoint.sh` fail loudly with a named reason below it, or keep 1.6 compatibility (preferred — nothing else in the tree needs 1.7). Run `run-checkpoint-derive.bats` and `run-checkpoint-record-round.bats` under jq 1.6 in CI.

---

## Observations

### 1. Fence — generic exec-flag check defeats the classifier for common consumers

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:363` — `_bdb_hd_re_exflag='^-[A-Za-z]*[cex][A-Za-z]*$'` (`:187`) is applied to every allowlisted consumer before its own grammar, so `jq -c`, `jq -e`, `jq -rc`, `yq -e`, `grep -c`, `grep -x`, `sed -n -e p`, `cat -e` and `echo -e` all classify `interpreter` and fall back to the full scan.
**Suggestion:** Apply the generic check only to consumers without a dedicated argv grammar, or whitelist the harmless short flags per command (`jq`/`yq`: `-c -e -r -S -s`; `grep`: `-c -x -E`) before the `[cex]` test. Add a corpus `allow` row for `jq -c '…' <<'EOF'` with a destructive string in the body.
**Benefit:** The #1245 false-positive class the classifier exists to remove still fires for the most common heredoc consumers in this codebase.

### 2. Karpathy hook — latency regression on every Write/Edit

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131` — the PostToolUse hook now forks `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` (bash + five jq calls, plus `br show` when beads is installed) and sources `profile-lib.sh` for two `loa_knob` reads on every Write/Edit/NotebookEdit. Measured on this host: head ≈ 280 ms per invocation without a checkpoint and ≈ 590 ms with one, versus ≈ 45 ms for the base hook; the hooks-reference budgets shell hooks at < 100 ms (`head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:229`).
**Suggestion:** Read the checkpoint task straight from `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` with one jq (the hook does not need the beads verification `read` performs), cache the two knob values in the summary file, or run the checkpoint lookup only when the summary's `task` is older than the state file's mtime.
**Benefit:** Keeps the per-tool-call hook cost inside the documented budget; the design note's "per-task files are small" argument does not account for the new fork.

### 3. Karpathy hook — the "task" key is the last closed bead, not the active one

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131-138` — `run-checkpoint.sh read --json` returns `.checkpoint.task` only when beads confirms that task is **closed** (otherwise it discards the checkpoint and returns `{checkpoint: null, sprint}`), so during implementation the key is either the bead that just closed or, whenever `br` is absent or the task is still open, the sprint. Reproduced: with `checkpoint.task = bd-1` and no `br`, the summary reads `"task":"sprint-1"`. `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:220` tells reviewers to read `.run/karpathy-surgical/<bead>.jsonl` for the sprint beads, which will hold the lines written while the *next* bead was in progress.
**Suggestion:** Key on the active bead (first open bead of the sprint from `br ready`, or `.checkpoint.task` without the closed-check) and say so in the hook header and in the reviewing-code SKILL line; or rename the key to `after-<bead>` so the reviewer reads it correctly.
**Benefit:** The SURGICAL axis attributes diff size to the right task.

### 4. Implement gate — the marker sanction is self-issuable through Bash

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh:545` — `check_implement_marker` sanctions every App-Zone write for two hours in every mode, including `deny`, on a `.run/implement-active.json` that `run-checkpoint.sh mark` (or a `printf` through the Bash tool) can create outside any run; the trust-input list only guards Write/Edit. The hooks-reference records this as an accepted gap (`:273`), so it is not blocking, but the `deny` documentation calls the gate "a fence only in this mode" without qualifying "against Write/Edit".
**Suggestion:** Have `mark` refuse when the derived cache is not RUNNING, or state the Write/Edit-only scope next to the word "fence" in the hook header and the reference.
**Benefit:** Operators turning on `deny` know what it does and does not fence.

### 5. Skill include — retrospective postlude passes no fallback

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/data/skill-includes/retrospective_postlude.md:1` — the include runs `profile-lib.sh knob invisible_retrospective.enabled` with no fallback, unlike `input_guardrails.md`. When `profiles.yaml` is missing or unreadable `loa_knob` falls to `_loa_pl_live` and prints the empty fallback, so the postlude silently never runs under the `standard` profile (whose value is `true`).
**Suggestion:** Pass the fallback (`knob invisible_retrospective.enabled true`) in the include and re-render the skills.
**Benefit:** The example's default survives a missing profiles file.

### 6. Karpathy hook — stale wording in the warning

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:193` — the warning still says "Session diff total" although the total is now per task; the state path it prints is the per-task file.
**Suggestion:** "Task diff total ${RUNNING} lines (task ${KEY}) exceeds …".
**Benefit:** The operator reading the warning is not told the wrong scope.

### 7. Fence — autostart content written through a non-executing consumer

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303` — `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` does not treat `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service`, `~/.config/autostart/*.desktop`, cron spool paths outside `/etc`, or a `Makefile` as executable content, so `cat <<'EOF' > ~/.config/systemd/user/x.service` with an `ExecStart=/bin/rm -rf …` body is `nonexec` and its body is dropped (verified with `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class`). The documented later-command gap covers the execution, but the targets are a short list worth adding.
**Suggestion:** Extend `_bdb_hd_re_sys` with `\.config/(systemd|autostart)/`, `(^|/)Makefile$`, `(^|/)GNUmakefile$`, `/var/spool/cron`.
**Benefit:** Closes the cheapest persistence targets without touching the grammar.

### 8. Process — implementation report and changelog

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `pr/PR.md:1` — the implementation report is the PR title plus "68 file(s) in scope"; there is no `## AC Verification` walkthrough, no per-task evidence, and the change touches no CHANGELOG. The task brief says the PR files are the whole input, so this is recorded rather than used as the automatic-fail trigger the skill prescribes.
**Suggestion:** Add the AC walkthrough (DEC-0140/0141/0143/0152/0161/0163/0166/0167/0168 each mapped to `file:line`) and a CHANGELOG entry per task before the audit.
**Benefit:** The audit gate can trace each decision to its evidence.

---

## Cross-Model Observations

Adversarial review ran with two voices (primary `gpt-5.5-pro` answered by `codex-headless`, companion `claude-headless`; `consensus_outcome: consensus`, 2/2 voices, `rejected_summary: []`). Triage:

## Changes Required

### 1. Security — heredoc classifier: same-command execution bypass of a floor fence

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608` — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` only recognises an executing reference when a later token's literal basename equals the heredoc target; a glob (`bash ./ru[n]`, `bash n.m?`), a pipe from a safe reader (`cat n.md | bash`), a process or command substitution (`bash <(cat n.md)`, `bash -c "$(cat n.md)"`), an indirect variable (`f=n.md; bash $f`) or a consumer that does not name the file (`make` after `cat > Makefile`) is missed, the heredoc stays `nonexec`, and `_bdb_hd_scan_body` (`:576`) drops every body line whose command word is not a fence verb. The written body then executes in the same command unseen.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:608-639` (`_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`), `:222-227` (`_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` lists `cat`, `git`, `gh`), `:576-600` (`_bdb_hd_scan_body`), `:538-574` (`_bdb_hd_segword` does not strip `if/then/do/else/elif/while/until` or case arms)
**Issue:** Reproduced end to end by feeding Bash-tool payloads to the head and base hooks (exit 0 = allow, 2 = block):

```
head=0 base=2 | cat > run <<'EOF' / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / bash ./ru[n]
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / echo pwned > .claude/settings.json / EOF / cat n.md | bash
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash <(cat n.md)
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / bash -c "$(cat n.md)"
head=0 base=2 | cat <<'EOF' > n.md / … / EOF / f=n.md; bash $f
head=0 base=2 | cat > Makefile <<'EOF' / all: / <tab>cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh / EOF / make
head=2 base=2 | control: … / EOF / bash n.md            (D119 shape, caught)
head=2 base=2 | control: body `rm -rf src` is kept as a fence-verb segment
```

The body content that disappears is exactly the class the fence-verb keep does not cover: `echo … > .claude/settings.json` (FR-SZ2-REDIR), `cp x .claude/hooks/x.sh` (FR-SZ-COPY), `tee`, `ln`, `sed -i` into the System Zone, and any destructive segment prefixed by a shell keyword (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `for f in src; do rm -rf $f; done` — both scrub to nothing, verified with `_bdb_heredoc_scrub`). FR-SZ and FR-SZ2 are `floor_guards` in `.claude/data/floor.yaml`; the hooks-reference "Remaining gap" (`head/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md:298`) covers only execution by a *later* command, so this is a regression inside the fence's own stated scope, not the documented gap.
**Why This Matters:** The classifier is on by default (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: true`). An autonomous agent that writes a helper file with a heredoc and runs it in the same command no longer has its body scanned, and the pre-cycle fence did scan it. The corpus (D119–D121) only covers the literal-basename shapes.
**Required Fix:** (1) In `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec`, treat any non-body line holding `$(`, a backtick, `<(` or `>(`, a glob character in a token, or a `$`-prefixed token as executing (return 0), mirroring `_bdb_hd_ctx_bad`; remove `cat`, `git` and `gh` from `_bdb_hd_is_safe_reader` when the segment is a pipeline member feeding an interpreter, or simply fall back to the full scan whenever any later segment's command word is an interpreter/wrapper (`_bdb_hd_is_interp`) regardless of whether it names the target. (2) In `_bdb_hd_segword`, strip the shell keywords (`if then else elif fi while until do done case esac select in coproc function`) and a leading case-arm pattern before reading the command word, or set `_hd_full=1` in `_bdb_hd_scan_body` when a segment's command word is a keyword. (3) Add corpus rows for each of the six shapes above (expect `block`) and for `cat <<EOF > notes.md` with an `if …; then rm -rf …; fi` body.
**Reference:** CWE-693 (Protection Mechanism Failure); the fence's own posture note (`hooks-reference.md:287`) accepts subshell wrapping as a bypass class for the *whole command*, not for a heredoc body the fence previously scanned.

### 2. Functionality — `run-checkpoint.sh derive` / `record-round` fail on jq 1.6

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378` — the per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and reads `$label` (`:380`, `:389`); `label` is a jq keyword and jq 1.6 rejects it (`syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__`), so `cmd_derive` exits 3 before producing any report, on every ledger.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378-395` and `:225-226`
**Issue:** Reproduced with the RCD-1 fixture (`bash -x`): `jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label … line 2: def mine: … $label` → `sj=` → exit 3. Minimal: `jq -n --arg label x '$label'` fails on jq-1.6 and works on 1.7. A second 1.6 incompatibility sits in `fb_parse` (`:225-226`): for a feedback file without a trailer `pj` is empty, and `jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj"` exits 0 on empty input under jq 1.6 (verified: `printf '' | jq -e 'type == "object"'; echo $?` → 0), so `pj` stays `""`, `--argjson p ''` fails with `invalid JSON text passed to --argjson`, `fb_parse` prints nothing and `record-round` exits 2 (`set -e`) on any legacy feedback file; `derive` would hit the same path on RCD-3. On a jq 1.6 host it is inert: every `run-checkpoint.sh write` and `mark` prints the derive error to stderr (`:174`, `:541`), `/loa`'s Run line is silently skipped, `/run-resume` step 0a gets exit 3 (its contract handles only 4), and the implement gate's `deny` mode never sees a `derived_at`, so it can only ever ask. **Required Fix:** Rename the binding (`--arg lbl` / `$lbl`, or `--arg local_label`) and avoid other jq keywords as variable names; replace the `jq -e` emptiness probe with an explicit test (`[[ -n "$pj" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' <<<"$pj" >/dev/null 2>&1 || pj='{}'`); either declare a jq ≥ 1.7 floor in the framework prerequisites and have `run-checkpoint.sh` fail loudly with a named reason below it, or keep 1.6 compatibility (preferred — nothing else in the tree needs 1.7). description: "Quirks of the /workspace PR-review environment that produce false test failures (noexec /tmp, jq 1.6, redacted fixtures, mount not at PR base)"

When reviewing a PR laid out under `/workspace/pr/{base,head,head.diff}` in this workspace (first seen 2026-10-23, task review-r20):

- `/tmp` is mounted `noexec`: any bats test that executes a script directly (not via `bash script`) fails with "Permission denied". Build overlay trees under `/home/evaluser/...` instead, and set `TMPDIR` there too.
- `pr/head` and `pr/base` files arrive with no executable bits; restore them from the diff's `100755` modes before running suites.
- The installed `jq` is 1.6: `$label` (jq keyword) is a syntax error and `jq -e` on empty input exits 0. Real portability defects, but check the repo's declared floor before rating.
- Fixture lines of the form `local secret="..."` are redacted to `local REDACTED-TEST-SECRET"` in both base and head copies (an eval artifact, not a PR defect); patch locally to run the suite.
- The `/workspace/.claude` checkout is not the PR's base revision for untouched files (e.g. `guard-yield.sh`, `golden-path.sh`, `adversarial-review-gate.sh`); when a PR suite fails on an untouched script, run the PR-base copy of the suite on the base tree before blaming the PR.
- Only files touched by the PR exist under `pr/`; suites needing other fixtures (`tests/fixtures/pretooluse-payloads/`, `constraint-rationales-pre-diet.json`, `guard-origins.bats`) fail for that reason alone.
- The live Bash fence blocks review commands whose *text* contains shapes like `> .claude/x` or `rm -rf /home/...`; write probe scripts with the Write tool under `/tmp` or `/home/evaluser` and run them by path.
- `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type review --sprint-id sprint-1 --diff-file pr/head.diff --context-file <concerns> --json` works here and takes about 10 minutes (two voices).

**Why:** Four of the five suite failures in the first pass were environment artifacts; separating them took most of the session.
**How to apply:** Set up the overlay in `/home/evaluser/rt/{head,base}` with exec bits and git identity first, then run suites once. Related: [[loa-review-sprint-pr-workflow]].

flatline_protocol:
  enabled: true
  auto_trigger: true
  phases:
    prd: true
    sdd: true
    sprint: true
  models:
    # 2026-10-01: claude-headless = Fable 5.1 on the CLI/Bedrock; `opus`/`fable` are http_api ids that fail
    # INVALID_CONFIG without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (fleet-measured, search 2026-10-01). Was opus.
    # Flatline runs its voices in parallel and nothing serialises CLI hops across it (the per-binary lock is
    # adversarial-review.sh's): two claude -p calls share the CLI and the plan window, each bounded by the catalog's
    # headless_timeout_seconds (900 s) — up to ~15 min per phase under contention (KF-037 / KF-038).
    # Its auth follows CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (the claude-bedrock wrapper for Bedrock, else the plain CLI's own login — bd-swz7), and it
    # shares the anthropic headless circuit breaker with the dissent companion: a rate limit on either opens it for both.
    # (thirty-seventh run, e2b DISS-C-002) so a Flatline rate limit leaves a review that follows while the breaker is open
    # single-voice: its companion is refused by the open breaker, the envelope reads companion_voice.status failed (not degraded),
    # and nothing in the unattended harness re-runs it (KF-038) — read companion_voice before taking such a review as two-voice.
    # (thirty-ninth run, e2b DISS-C-002/003) the route — and the account billed — is the environment's, not this file's: a shell
    # without CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN (cron, CI, a fresh login) runs Flatline and Bridgebuilder on the plain CLI's plan, and the breaker
    # bucket is anthropic/headless whatever the route, so a plan-window limit there also refuses a Bedrock-wrapped companion; export
    # the wrapper in every shell that runs them, and clear a bucket opened on the other route with `cheval --reset-breaker anthropic:headless`.
    primary: claude-headless
    # cycle-109 substrate-debug (2026-05-13): switched secondary from gpt-5.5-pro
    # to gpt-5.5 (non-pro). Direct probe of current OpenAI key showed it lacks
    # Pro-tier access (gpt-5.5-pro → 404 "not a chat model" on /v1/chat/completions
    # AND insufficient_quota on /v1/responses; gpt-5.5 → success with correct
    # params). gpt-5.5 is the cost-safe default per cycle-095 Sprint 2; alias
    # already in substrate catalog. Filed as cycle-109 evidence (C109.OP-6):
    # substrate misdiagnosed model-tier-access-denied as insufficient_quota —
    # FR-1 capability-aware substrate would have caught this at boot.
    secondary: gpt-5.5
    # cycle-124 (2026-09-17): tertiary DISABLED on this host — gemini CLI is tier-blocked (KF-018, rec 2) and
    # hounfour.headless.mode cli-only never reaches the HTTP rung, so a configured tertiary only turns every
    # Flatline run into 2/3 DEGRADED (Phase 2 skipped). Fleet baseline (framework-review §10): no tertiary
    # unless `agy` is installed. Re-enable by restoring the line below.
    # tertiary: gemini-3.1-pro # cheval bare-alias (resolves to API id gemini-3.1-pro-preview); was gemini-3.1-pro-preview which is not a valid cheval alias — see cycle-102 flatline-prd-degradation.md
  thresholds:
    high_consensus: 700
    disputed_delta: 300
    low_value: 400
    blocker_skeptic: 700
  max_iterations: 5
  # Phase 2.5: Adversarial cross-model review (PR #552 enforcement gate)
  # When enabled, `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint` invoke a cross-model
  # dissenter (gpt-5.3-codex by default) and produce adversarial-{review,audit}.json.
  # The PreToolUse:Write hook at .claude/hooks/safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh
  # blocks COMPLETED marker writes when enabled but the artifact is missing.
  # Emergency override: LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false.
  code_review:
    enabled: true
    # cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.9 (2026-05-12): REVERTED to gpt-5.5-pro per
    # SDD R8. Closing evidence:
    #   (1) Architecture proof — chain_resolver populates the within-
    #       company chain `gpt-5.5-pro → gpt-5.5 → gpt-5.3-codex → codex-headless`
    #       and cheval.cmd_invoke walks it on EmptyContentError. Pinned by
    #       .claude/adapters/tests/test_chain_walk_audit_envelope.py
    #       (test_primary_empty_content_walks_to_fallback mocks the
    #       primary returning EMPTY_CONTENT and asserts walk to fallback).
    #   (2) Empirical evidence — cycle-104 sprint-2 T2.10 25-trial live
    #       replay (2026-05-12) showed KF-003 NOT REPRODUCIBLE at OpenAI
    #       across 5 sizes × 5 prompts at 30K-80K input tokens.
    # The T1B.4 workaround is no longer load-bearing. If KF-003 returns,
    # the chain absorbs it; if the chain exhausts, T2.8 voice-drop keeps
    # consensus available with the remaining voices. gpt-5.5-pro restores
    # cross-model dissent diversity per cycle-102 §G2 rationale.
    # Original cycle-102 T1B.4 swap comment retained in git history.

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and
  `budget_cents` is a per-voice cap (a malformed cap is 0 cents — the run fails closed with `status: budget_exceeded`).
  Findings carry `voice` (the outer hop, matching `final_model`) and `answered_by` (the model that produced them);
  `companion_voice.answered_by` is the companion's own succeeded id. An operator may set
  `flatline_protocol.<block>.companion_chain: {anthropic: [...], openai: [...]}` to replace the default chains of D-2.1

  is `reason: prompt_copy_failed` (no fork). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR=1` keeps the `/tmp` workdir's files, never a
  process.
- **`companion_voice.independent` / `counted_as`.** Independence compares the two `answered_by` families (the primary's
  succeeded id, not its configured hop). Same family — or either family `unknown`, an id no catalog entry or name rule
  places, which is no evidence of a second family: the companion's findings are kept (tagged) but its envelope
  contributes no voice to verdict quality — `counted_as: duplicate_voice` (the aggregator counts distinct voices; its
  INV-5 forbids one id both succeeded and dropped, so a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's succeeded voices
  feeds no dropped-voice envelope either, and a MIXED attempt envelope keeps its own voice: a copy without the conflicting
  dropped entry is aggregated — `primary_attempts_rewritten` / `companion_attempts_rewritten`; an envelope with no
  succeeded voice that dropped the other side's voice is excluded — `primary_attempts_excluded` /
  `companion_attempts_excluded`). A primary that never answered leaves the companion `counted_as: sole_voice`

  `degraded: true`, `primary_voice: {status: failed}`) so the completed voice is never buried. An aggregator failure is
  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar

  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's

  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed

  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are

  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.

**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).
KF-004 evidence: the three real rejected payloads under `tests/fixtures/dissent-rejected/` now pass without a repair.

## Numeric anchors and the budget scaling (cycle-131 FR-4)

- **Numeric anchors (`anchor_line`, `anchor_line_end`).** Both prompts ask each voice for the head-file line the finding
  sits on (`anchor_line`) and, for a range, its last line (`anchor_line_end`), beside the symbol `anchor` and
  `anchor_type`. The symbol anchor stays the stable reference and stays required for high-severity findings: the
  anchor check, `anchor_stability` and the hallucination filter key on `anchor` alone. The normaliser keeps a line only
  as a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000, and an end only beside a kept start and at least it; any other value is
  dropped silently, never a rejection or a repair hop. A finding with no line is unchanged. Graders (the eval harness's
  envelope reduction) read `anchor_line` with the anchor's file as `path:line[-end]`; read them as a pointer, never as
  a replacement for the symbol.
- **Budget scaling (`budget_scale`, `budget_cents_max`).** `flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale`
  is `fixed` (the default; an absent key is the shipped gate, byte for byte) or `diff`: the budget becomes
  `min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)` (`budget_cents_max` default 600), where the estimate
  is the gate's own pre-dispatch estimate over the planned voices. An estimate above that budget still refuses (exit 4,
  `status: budget_exceeded`, `reason: budget`). A malformed scale or maximum is said and `fixed` applies. When the key is
  written, the envelope's metadata carries `budget_scale`, `budget_cents_effective` and `budget_cents_max`. The eval
  harness writes `diff` for both gates in its sandbox config; the shipped default stays `fixed`.

#!/bin/bash
# Check audit prerequisites
# Usage: ./check-audit-prerequisites.sh sprint-1

AUDIT_TYPE="$1"
SPRINT_ID="$2"

case "$AUDIT_TYPE" in
    "sprint")
        if [[ ! "$SPRINT_ID" =~ ^sprint-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "ERROR: Invalid sprint ID format"
            exit 1
        fi

        FEEDBACK_FILE="grimoires/loa/a2a/${SPRINT_ID}/engineer-feedback.md"
        if [ ! -f "$FEEDBACK_FILE" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: No engineer feedback file - sprint must be reviewed first"
            exit 1
        fi

        if ! grep -q "All good" "$FEEDBACK_FILE"; then
            echo "ERROR: Sprint not approved by senior lead"
            exit 1
        fi

        echo "PREREQUISITES_MET"
        ;;

    "deployment")
        if [ ! -d "grimoires/loa/deployment" ]; then
            echo "ERROR: No deployment directory found"
            exit 1
        fi

        echo "PREREQUISITES_MET"
        ;;

    "codebase")
        echo "PREREQUISITES_MET"
        ;;

    *)
        echo "ERROR: Unknown audit type. Use: sprint, deployment, codebase"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |

   123	# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
   124	# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
   125	cfg() {
   126	  local v
   127	  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
   128	    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
   129	    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
   130	  else
   131	    printf 'null'
   132	  fi

   134	cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
   135	  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")

   139	_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

   141	# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
   142	# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
   143	# previous file is untouched.
   144	atomic_update() {
   145	  local f="$1"; shift
   146	  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
   147	  (
   148	    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
   149	    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
   150	    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
   151	    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
   152	      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
   153	    else
   154	      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
   155	    fi
   156	    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
   157	    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
   158	  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
   159	  return $rc
   160	}

   162	cmd_write() {
   163	  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
   164	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
   165	  local ts rc=0
   166	  ts=$(now_iso)
   167	  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
   168	    '.schema_version = 2
   169	     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
   170	     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
   171	  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
   172	  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
   173	  local err drc=0
   174	  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?

   179	bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
   180	  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
   181	  local js st
   182	  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   183	  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
   184	  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]

   187	cmd_read() {
   188	  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
   189	  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return 0; fi
   190	  local sv cp s t p ts reason="" brc
   191	  sv=$(jq -r '.schema_version // 1' "$file"); cp=$(jq -c '.checkpoint // null' "$file")
   192	  [[ "$sv" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || sv=1
   193	  if [[ "$cp" == "null" || "$sv" -lt 2 ]]; then
   194	    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi
   195	    return 0
   196	  fi
   197	  s=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.sprint // empty' "$file"); t=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.task // empty' "$file"); p=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.phase // empty' "$file"); ts=$(jq -r '.checkpoint.ts // empty' "$file")

   199	  elif [[ -n "$t" ]]; then
   200	    # A task checkpoint is trusted only when beads CONFIRMS the task closed;
   201	    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).
   202	    brc=0; bead_closed "$t" || brc=$?
   203	    case $brc in 0) ;; 2) reason="beads unavailable — task $t cannot be verified";; *) reason="task $t is not closed in beads";; esac
   204	  fi
   205	  if [[ -n "$reason" ]]; then
   206	    echo "run-checkpoint: discarding checkpoint ($reason) — resume from the first open bead of $s" >&2
   207	    if (( json )); then jq -cn --arg r "$reason" --arg s "$s" '{checkpoint:null, reason:$r, sprint:$s}'; else echo "checkpoint: discarded ($reason); resume at the first open bead of $s"; fi
   208	    return 0
   209	  fi
   210	  if (( json )); then jq -c '{checkpoint: .checkpoint}' "$file"
   211	  else echo "checkpoint: $s ${t:+task $t }phase $p at $ts → resume at the first open bead after $t in $s"; fi
   212	}

   214	# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
   215	# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
   216	# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
   217	# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
   218	fb_parse() {
   219	  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
   220	  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
   221	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
   222	  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
   223	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
   224	  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
   225	  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
   226	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
   227	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
   228	    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
   229	  else
   230	    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
   231	  fi
   232	  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
   233	    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
   234	    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
   235	    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
   236	     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
   237	     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
   238	     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
   239	    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
   240	}

   242	# impl_commit SINCE → "sha epoch" of the newest non-merge commit on HEAD since
   243	# SINCE touching a path outside the state/generated set, or nothing
   244	impl_commit() {
   245	  git -C "$root" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
   246	  git -C "$root" log --no-merges -n 1 --format='%H %ct' ${1:+"--since=$1"} -- . \
   247	    ':(exclude,glob)grimoires/**' ':(exclude,glob).run/**' ':(exclude,glob)**/REPO-MAP.md' \
   248	    ':(exclude,glob)**/checksums.json' ':(exclude,glob)**/CHANGELOG.md' 2>/dev/null || true
   249	}

   251	# The ordered rounds of one sprint directory: every -rN file, then the current
   252	# file unless it is byte-identical to the highest -rN of its gate
   253	rounds_of() {
   254	  local dir="$1" g base f n top topn cur
   255	  for g in review audit; do
   256	    if [[ "$g" == review ]]; then base=engineer-feedback; else base=auditor-sprint-feedback; fi
   257	    top=""; topn=-1
   258	    for f in "$dir/$base"-r*.md; do
   259	      [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   260	      n=${f##*-r}; n=${n%.md}
   261	      [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,6}$ ]] || continue
   262	      fb_parse "$f" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" --argjson n "$((10#$n))" '. + {gate: $g, round: $n}'
   263	      if (( 10#$n > topn )); then topn=$((10#$n)); top="$f"; fi
   264	    done
   265	    cur="$dir/$base.md"
   266	    if [[ -f "$cur" ]] && ! { [[ -n "$top" ]] && cmp -s "$cur" "$top"; }; then
   267	      fb_parse "$cur" "$g" | jq -c --arg g "$g" '. + {gate: $g, round: 999999}'
   268	    fi
   269	  done
   270	}

   272	# Shared jq definitions: time, the breaker recompute and the run-state resolution
   273	JQ_DEFS='
   274	def epoch: if type == "string" then (sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) else null end;
   275	def fresh($now; $win): epoch as $t | $t != null and ($now - $t) <= $win and ($t - $now) <= 300;
   276	def recompute($rounds; $reset):
   277	  ($rounds
   278	   | map(select($reset == null or ((.ts // "") > $reset)))
   279	   | sort_by([(.ts // ""), .round, (if .gate == "review" then 0 else 1 end)])
   280	   | map(select(.approved | not))) as $nr
   281	  | reduce $nr[] as $r ({cycle: 0, same: 0, hash: null, np: 0, lc: null};
   282	      .cycle += 1
   283	      | (if $r.hash != "none" and $r.hash == .hash then .same += 1 else .same = 1 | .hash = $r.hash end)
   284	      | ($r.counts | tojson) as $c
   285	      | (if .lc != null and .lc == $c then .np += 1 else .np = 0 end)
   286	      | .lc = $c);
   287	def skeleton($th; $ts):
   288	  {state: "CLOSED",
   289	   triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: $th.same, last_hash: null},
   290	              no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: $th.np},
   291	              cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: $th.cycles},
   292	              timeout: {started: $ts, limit_hours: $th.hours}},
   293	   history: []};
   294	def merge_breaker($rc; $th; $ts):
   295	  (if type == "object" then . else skeleton($th; $ts) end)
   296	  | .triggers = (.triggers // {})
   297	  | .triggers.cycle_count.current = ([(.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0), $rc.cycle] | max)
   298	  | (if $rc.same > (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0)
   299	     then .triggers.same_issue.count = $rc.same | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = $rc.hash else . end)
   300	  | (if $rc.np > (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) or (.triggers.no_progress.last_counts == null and $rc.lc != null)
   301	     then .triggers.no_progress.count = ([(.triggers.no_progress.count // 0), $rc.np] | max)
   302	          | .triggers.no_progress.last_counts = $rc.lc else . end)
   303	  | ( if (.triggers.same_issue.count // 0) >= (.triggers.same_issue.threshold // $th.same)
   304	        then ["same_issue", "same issue hash repeated \(.triggers.same_issue.count) times (derived from the feedback history)"]
   305	      elif (.triggers.no_progress.count // 0) >= (.triggers.no_progress.threshold // $th.np)
   306	        then ["no_progress", "counts unchanged for \(.triggers.no_progress.count) consecutive rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   307	      elif (.triggers.cycle_count.current // 0) >= (.triggers.cycle_count.limit // $th.cycles)
   308	        then ["cycle_count", "\(.triggers.cycle_count.current) changes-required rounds (derived from the feedback history)"]
   309	      else null end ) as $trip
   310	  | if $trip != null and (.state // "CLOSED") != "OPEN"
   311	    then .state = "OPEN" | .history = ((.history // []) + [{timestamp: $ts, trigger: $trip[0], reason: $trip[1], source: "derive"}])
   312	    else .state = (.state // "CLOSED") end;
   313	def known_ids: (.derivation.sprint_ids // null) // ((.sprints.list // []) | map(.id? // empty));
   314	def resolve($f; $now; $win):
   315	  . as $c
   316	  | (if ($c | type) == "object" then $c else {} end) as $c
   317	  | ($c.state // $c.status // "") as $cs
   318	  | ($c | known_ids) as $known
   319	  | ([$f.sprints[] | select(.state != "complete")
   320	      | "sprint-\(.global_id)" as $g | .local_label as $l
   321	      | select(($known | index($g)) == null and ($l == "" or ($known | index($l)) == null))] | length > 0) as $new
   322	  | ((($c.completion // {}) | .merged_sha? // "") | type == "string" and length > 0) as $merged
   323	  | if ($c.state // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or ($c.status // "") == "JACKED_OUT" or $merged then "JACKED_OUT"
   324	    elif $f.breaker_open or $cs == "HALTED" then "HALTED"
   325	    elif $f.all_complete then "COMPLETE"
   326	    elif $cs == "COMPLETE" and ($new | not) then "COMPLETE"
   327	    elif ($c.timestamps.last_activity? // null) | fresh($now; $win) then "RUNNING"
   328	    else "INTERRUPTED" end;
   329	'

   331	cmd_derive() {
   332	  local ledger="$root/grimoires/loa/ledger.json" a2a="$root/grimoires/loa/a2a" active rows
   333	  if [[ ! -f "$ledger" ]] || ! jq -e 'type == "object"' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   334	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: no readable ledger at $ledger — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   335	  fi
   336	  active=$(jq -r '.active_cycle // empty | strings' "$ledger")
   337	  if [[ -z "$active" ]] || ! jq -e --arg c "$active" 'any(.cycles[]?; .id == $c)' "$ledger" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   338	    echo "run-checkpoint: derive: the ledger has no active cycle — callers keep the cache" >&2; return 4
   339	  fi
   340	  local win now now_ts fa=1 th
   341	  win=$(( $(cfg_int '.run_mode.stale_hours' 12 8760) * 3600 ))
   342	  [[ "$(cfg '.run_mode.file_authoritative')" == false ]] && fa=0
   343	  th=$(jq -nc --argjson s "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.same_issue_threshold' 3 1000)" \
   344	              --argjson n "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.circuit_breaker.no_progress_threshold' 5 1000)" \
   345	              --argjson c "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.max_cycles' 20 10000)" \
   346	              --argjson h "$(cfg_int '.run_mode.defaults.timeout_hours' 8 8760)" \
   347	              '{same: $s, np: $n, cycles: $c, hours: $h}')
   348	  now=$(date +%s); now_ts=$(now_iso)
   349	
   350	  # Per-sprint facts
   351	  local sprints="[]" gid label lstatus since dir rv au mex msid ic sj
   352	  rows=$(jq -r --arg c "$active" '
   353	    (.cycles[] | select(.id == $c)) as $cy
   354	    | ($cy.sprints // [])[]
   355	    | select((.global_id | type) == "number")
   356	    | [(.global_id | tostring), ((.local_label // "") | tostring), ((.status // "") | tostring),
   357	       ([.started, .created, $cy.created] | map(select(type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-")))
   358	        | if length == 0 then "" else ([.[0], ($cy.created // "")] | max) end)]
   359	    | map(if . == "" then "-" else . end)
   360	    | @tsv' "$ledger")
   361	  # "-" stands for an empty field: IFS whitespace (tab) would collapse two adjacent separators
   362	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r gid label lstatus since; do
   363	    [[ "$gid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
   364	    [[ "$label" == - ]] && label=""
   365	    [[ "$since" == - ]] && since=""
   366	    [[ "$label" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$ ]] || label=""
   367	    [[ "$lstatus" =~ ^[a-z_]{1,32}$ ]] || lstatus="unknown"
   368	    [[ "$since" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$ ]] || since=""
   369	    dir="$a2a/sprint-$gid"
   370	    rv=$(fb_parse "$dir/engineer-feedback.md" review)
   371	    au=$(fb_parse "$dir/auditor-sprint-feedback.md" audit)
   372	    mex=false; msid=""
   373	    if [[ -f "$dir/COMPLETED" ]]; then
   374	      mex=true
   375	      msid=$(sed -n 's/^sprint:[[:space:]]*\([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\).*/\1/p' "$dir/COMPLETED" | head -n 1) || msid=""
   376	    fi
   377	    ic=$(impl_commit "$since")
   378	    sj=$(jq -nc --argjson gid "$gid" --arg label "$label" --arg status "$lstatus" --argjson rv "$rv" --argjson au "$au" \
   379	              --argjson mex "$mex" --arg msid "$msid" --arg ic "$ic" '
   380	      def mine: type == "string" and length > 0 and (. == "sprint-\($gid)" or ($label != "" and . == $label));
   381	      ($rv.approved == true and ($rv.sprint_id | mine)) as $R
   382	      | ($au.approved == true and ($au.sprint_id | mine)) as $A
   383	      | ([$rv.sprint_id, $au.sprint_id, (if $msid == "" then null else $msid end)] | map(select(type == "string" and length > 0))) as $ids
   384	      | ($mex and any($ids[]; mine | not)) as $stale
   385	      | ($mex and ($stale | not) and (($rv.sprint_id | mine) or ($au.sprint_id | mine))) as $M
   386	      | ($ic | split(" ")) as $c
   387	      | ([$rv.ts, $au.ts] | map(select(. != null)) | max) as $vts
   388	      | def verdict($x): if $x.exists then {verdict: $x.verdict, sprint_id: $x.sprint_id, consistent: ($x.exit_code == 0), file: $x.file} else null end;
   389	      {global_id: $gid, local_label: $label, status: $status,
   390	       completed_marker: $M, marker_present: $mex, stale_marker: $stale,
   391	       review: verdict($rv), audit: verdict($au),
   392	       impl_commit: (if ($c | length) == 2 then $c[0] else null end),
   393	       commit_after_verdict: (if ($c | length) == 2 and $vts != null
   394	                              then (($c[1] | tonumber) > ($vts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch 0)) else null end),
   395	       legacy_feedback: ([$rv, $au] | map(select(.exists and (.trailer | not)) | .file)),
   396	       state: (if $M and $R and $A and $status == "completed" then "complete"
   397	               elif ($M | not) and $R and $A then "awaiting_marker" else "in_progress" end)}')
   398	    sprints=$(jq -c --argjson s "$sj" '. + [$s]' <<<"$sprints")
   399	  done <<<"$rows"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# run-checkpoint.sh — run position in .run/ (cycle-125 FR-3, SDD D-3.2;
# cycle-129 FR-4(f)/FR-5, SDD D-4.6, D-5.1 … D-5.4). Beads are the task ledger;
# the checkpoint is a HINT; the run state and the breaker are caches DERIVED
# from files (COMPLETED markers, LOA-VERDICT trailers, the ledger, git).
#
#   run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --phase PHASE [--task BEAD-ID] [--file F]
#       Atomically sets .schema_version = 2, .checkpoint = {sprint, task, phase, ts}
#       and .timestamps.last_activity = ts: jq → F.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock
#       on F.lock. F must already exist (a run in progress). Then runs
#       `derive --write` (a missing ledger is skipped). Exit 0 · 2 usage /
#       no run · 3 write failed (the previous file is untouched).
#   run-checkpoint.sh read [--file F] [--json]
#       Prints the checkpoint when it is trustworthy: parses, and when a task
#       is named, `br show <task> --json` reports it closed (a checkpoint that
#       names an open or unknown bead is DISCARDED with a logged line — beads
#       remain the recovery source). schema_version 1 / no checkpoint → prints
#       "sprint granularity". Exit 0 always when F exists; 2 when it does not.
#   run-checkpoint.sh derive [--json] [--write] [--root DIR] [--file F]
#       For the ledger's active cycle, per sprint: global_id, local_label,
#       ledger status, completed_marker (a2a/sprint-<gid>/COMPLETED exists and
#       the feedback trailers name this sprint, as sprint-<gid> or the local
#       label; a trailer or a `sprint:` line naming another sprint makes it a
#       stale_marker, treated as absent), review/audit verdicts (verdict-derive.sh;
#       APPROVED needs exit 0; a file without a trailer is legacy: no verdict,
#       listed in derivation.legacy_feedback), impl_commit (newest non-merge
#       commit on HEAD since max(sprint started|created, cycle created) touching
#       a path outside grimoires/, .run/, REPO-MAP.md, checksums.json,
#       CHANGELOG.md) and state complete | awaiting_marker | in_progress.
#       Run state, first match wins:
#         cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha → JACKED_OUT (terminal)
#         breaker OPEN, or cache HALTED                                 → HALTED (sticky until /run-resume)
#         every sprint complete                                         → COMPLETE
#         cache COMPLETE and the ledger registers no new incomplete sprint → COMPLETE
#         last_activity within run_mode.stale_hours (12)                → RUNNING
#         otherwise                                                     → INTERRUPTED
#       Breaker (active sprint = first incomplete, else the last): the ordered
#       rounds engineer-feedback-r*.md, auditor-sprint-feedback-r*.md and the
#       current files (sorted by trailer ts, round, gate; rounds before the
#       breaker's reset_at are ignored) give cycle_count (non-APPROVED rounds),
#       same_issue (consecutive equal hashes) and no_progress (consecutive
#       equal counts); each cached counter is raised to its recomputed value,
#       never lowered; OPEN when a count threshold is met (timeout is left to
#       record-round). --json prints the derivation; --write rewrites F
#       (.state canonical, .status mirrored, derived_at, derivation {source,
#       stale_markers, legacy_feedback, sprint_ids}; schema_version kept) and
#       the breaker, under their locks — only when F exists, parses, and
#       run_mode.file_authoritative is not false (false = report-only).
#       Exit 0 · 4 no ledger / no active cycle · 2 usage.
#   run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file FEEDBACK [--sprint sprint-N]
#                                  [--state-file F] [--breaker B]
#       After a review or audit: verdict-derive.sh --json on FEEDBACK; the
#       same-issue hash is md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` of that output
#       (no trailer: md5 of the first 50 lines from ## Findings / ## Issues /
#       ## Changes Required). APPROVED (exit 0) leaves every counter as is.
#       Otherwise, atomically on B: same_issue +1 when the hash equals
#       last_hash, else count 1 and last_hash = hash; no_progress +1 when the
#       counts equal the previous round's, else 0; cycle_count.current +1; then
#       the triggers in order same_issue ≥ threshold, no_progress ≥ threshold,
#       cycle_count ≥ limit, timeout (now - started ≥ limit_hours). A trip sets
#       state OPEN, appends history {timestamp, trigger, reason, gate, sprint},
#       sets F (.run/state.json) .state = HALTED, prints
#       `TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` and exits 10 (also when B is already OPEN).
#       Exit 0 recorded · 2 usage / missing file · 3 write failed · 10 tripped.
#   run-checkpoint.sh mark --skill implement|bug --sprint ID [--root DIR]
#       Writes .run/implement-active.json {skill, sprint, started_at} (the
#       implement gate's marker sanction, valid two hours), then runs
#       `derive --write` when F exists. `unmark` removes the marker. Exit 0 · 2 usage.
#
# Default F: $LOA_RUN_DIR/sprint-plan-state.json, else <root>/.run/sprint-plan-state.json
# (--root DIR sets <root> and ignores LOA_RUN_DIR). B: <run dir>/circuit-breaker.json.
# Readers accept schema_version 1 and 2 and files without derived_at/derivation.
# Config (<root>/.loa.config.yaml, yq; absent = defaults): run_mode.stale_hours (12),
# run_mode.file_authoritative (true), run_mode.circuit_breaker.{same_issue,no_progress}_threshold
# (3, 5), run_mode.defaults.{max_cycles,timeout_hours} (20, 8) for a new breaker file.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
export LC_ALL=C
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
VERDICT_DERIVE="$SCRIPT_DIR/verdict-derive.sh"
usage() { sed -n '3,/^# Default F/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }

sub="${1:-}"; [[ -n "$sub" ]] || usage; shift
file="" sprint="" task="" phase="" json=0 write=0 root="" gate="" state_file="" breaker="" skill=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --file)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --sprint) [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; sprint="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --task)   [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ ]] || usage; task="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --phase)  [[ $# -ge 2 && "$2" =~ ^[A-Z_]+$ ]] || usage; phase="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --json)   json=1; shift ;;
    --write)  write=1; shift ;;
    --root)   [[ $# -ge 2 && -d "${2:-}" ]] || usage; root="$(cd "$2" && pwd)"; shift 2 ;;
    --gate)   [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == review || "$2" == audit ) ]] || usage; gate="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --state-file|--file-state) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; state_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --breaker) [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage; breaker="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skill)  [[ $# -ge 2 && ( "$2" == implement || "$2" == bug ) ]] || usage; skill="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

# Root and run dir: --root wins (and pins the run dir under it); else the
# directory holding a --file that sits in a .run/ dir (write/read/derive only);
# else this script's checkout with $LOA_RUN_DIR honoured.
if [[ -n "$root" ]]; then
  run_dir="$root/.run"
else
  root="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  run_dir="${LOA_RUN_DIR:-$root/.run}"
  if [[ -n "$file" && "$sub" != record-round ]]; then
    fdir="$(cd "$(dirname "$file")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || fdir=""
    if [[ -n "$fdir" && "$(basename "$fdir")" == .run ]]; then root="$(dirname "$fdir")"; run_dir="$fdir"; fi
  fi
fi
if [[ "$sub" != record-round && -z "$file" ]]; then file="$run_dir/sprint-plan-state.json"; fi
[[ -n "$breaker" ]] || breaker="$run_dir/circuit-breaker.json"
[[ -n "$state_file" ]] || state_file="$run_dir/state.json"
CONFIG="$root/.loa.config.yaml"

now_iso() { date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ; }

# cfg KEY → the raw yq value ("null" when absent or unreadable). yq's `//`
# treats false as absent, so callers compare the raw text.
cfg() {
  local v
  if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$CONFIG" ]]; then
    v=$(yq "$1" "$CONFIG" 2>/dev/null) || v="null"
    printf '%s' "${v//\"/}"
  else
    printf 'null'
  fi
}
cfg_int() {  # KEY DEFAULT MAX → a positive integer ≤ MAX, else DEFAULT
  local v; v=$(cfg "$1")
  if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( v > 0 && v <= $3 )); then printf '%s' "$v"; else printf '%s' "$2"; fi
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

# atomic_update FILE JQ-ARGS... — jq over FILE (or {} when FILE is absent) →
# FILE.tmp.$$ → mv -f, under flock on FILE.lock. Exit 3 on any failure; the
# previous file is untouched.
atomic_update() {
  local f="$1"; shift
  local tmp="$f.tmp.$$" rc=0
  (
    # flock is util-linux (Linux); without it (macOS) the write is still atomic
    # (tmp + mv) but concurrent writers may interleave — last writer wins.
    if command -v flock >/dev/null 2>&1; then flock -w 5 9 || { echo "run-checkpoint: lock timeout on $f.lock" >&2; exit 3; }; fi
    if [[ -f "$f" ]]; then
      jq "$@" "$f" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: $f is not valid JSON — not written" >&2; exit 3; }
    else
      jq "$@" <<<'{}' > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: could not build $f" >&2; exit 3; }
    fi
    jq -e . "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { rm -f -- "$tmp"; echo "run-checkpoint: refusing to replace $f with unparseable output" >&2; exit 3; }
    mv -f -- "$tmp" "$f"
  ) 9>"$f.lock" || rc=$?
  return $rc
}

cmd_write() {
  [[ -n "$sprint" && -n "$phase" ]] || usage
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file (start a run first)" >&2; return 2; fi
  local ts rc=0
  ts=$(now_iso)
  atomic_update "$file" --arg s "$sprint" --arg t "$task" --arg p "$phase" --arg ts "$ts" \
    '.schema_version = 2
     | .checkpoint = {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: $p, ts: $ts}
     | .timestamps = ((.timestamps // {}) + {last_activity: $ts})' || rc=$?
  (( rc == 0 )) || return $rc
  # Every checkpoint refreshes the derived caches (D-5.2); a missing ledger (4) is not an error here
  local err drc=0
  err=$( { write=1; json=0; cmd_derive >/dev/null; } 2>&1 ) || drc=$?
  if (( drc != 0 && drc != 4 )); then printf '%s\n' "$err" >&2; fi
  return 0
}

bead_closed() {  # $1 bead id → 0 when br reports closed
  command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 2
  local js st
  js=$(br show "$1" --json 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  st=$(printf '%s' "$js" | jq -r 'if type=="array" then .[0] else . end | .status // .issue.status // empty' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ "$st" == "closed" ]]
}

cmd_read() {
  if [[ ! -f "$file" ]]; then echo "run-checkpoint: no run state at $file" >&2; return 2; fi
  if ! jq -e . "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "run-checkpoint: $file unparseable — no checkpoint; beads are the recovery truth" >&2; if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"unparseable"}'; fi; return

    if (( json )); then echo '{"checkpoint":null,"reason":"sprint granularity"}'; else echo "checkpoint: none (schema_version $sv → sprint granularity; resume at the first open bead of sprints.current)"; fi

    # "br unavailable" is not a confirmation (Bridgebuilder PR #1269 FIND-003).

# fb_parse FILE GATE → one compact JSON object: {file, exists, trailer, verdict,
# counts, exit_code, sprint_id, ts, approved, hash}. The hash is the run-mode
# same-issue hash (md5 of `jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}'` over verdict-derive's
# --json output; legacy files hash their findings section).
fb_parse() {
  local f="$1" g="$2" rel vj tl pj hash
  rel="${f#"$root"/}"
  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then jq -nc --arg f "$rel" '{file: $f, exists: false}'; return 0; fi
  vj=$(bash "$VERDICT_DERIVE" --file "$f" --gate "$g" --json 2>/dev/null) || true
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$vj" || vj='{"trailer_found":false,"verdict":null,"counts":null,"exit_code":1}'
  tl=$(grep -E '^<!-- LOA-VERDICT \{.*\} -->[[:space:]]*$' "$f" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1) || tl=""
  pj=$(printf '%s' "$tl" | sed -E 's/^<!-- LOA-VERDICT (.*) -->[[:space:]]*$/\1/')
  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$pj" || pj='{}'
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.trailer_found' <<<"$vj")" == true ]]; then
    hash=$(printf '%s\n' "$vj" | jq -Sc '{verdict,counts}' | _md5)
  else
    hash=$( { grep -A 100 "## Findings\|## Issues\|## Changes Required" "$f" 2>/dev/null || true; } | head -50 | _md5)
  fi
  jq -nc --arg f "$rel" --argjson v "$vj" --argjson p "$pj" --arg h "$hash" '
    def sid: if type == "string" and test("^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$") then . else null end;
    def tsv: if type == "string" and test("^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:.]+Z$") then . else null end;
    {file: $f, exists: true, trailer: ($v.trailer_found == true),
     verdict: ($v.verdict | if type == "string" then . else null end),
     counts: ($v.counts // null), exit_code: ($v.exit_code // 1),
     sprint_id: ($p.sprint_id | sid), ts: ($p.ts | tsv), hash: $h}
    | .approved = (.exit_code == 0 and .verdict == "APPROVED")'
}

rounds_of() {
